content.comment_body: I have two identical electrical panels. I created a program for [product_name] and [product_name] HMI. The first panel operates properly. For the second panel, I programmed it through a router (connecting [product_name], [product_name] HMI, and PC), and it worked as expected. After disconnecting the Ethernet cables from the router and using only one cable between [product_name] and the HMI, the LED Link indicator turned off. I attempted to connect with different Ethernet cables—which work on the first panel for direct connection to [product_name]—but there was no change. Changing IP and default gateway also didn't help. I tried rebooting by turning the power off and on after waiting a few seconds, but that had no effect. Diagnostics reported a "Network error." My guess is there is something wrong with the Ethernet port. I checked the documentation but couldn't find any useful hints. Does anyone have suggestions? The program on [product_name] runs as expected and executes its logic correctly.

Hello everyone! The problem turned out to be hardware-related. I discovered that one pin in the Ethernet port had completely broken off and another pin was partially detached. This was clearly a manufacturing defect.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered an Ethernet communication issue between a [product_name] module and an HMI, with diagnostics indicating a network error despite correct program execution. Investigation revealed the problem was caused by defective pins in the device's Ethernet port, indicating a factory hardware fault.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable Ethernet connectivity between [product_name] and HMI devices, with fully functional hardware ports, and wishes for documentation that provides effective troubleshooting advice.
